annotationRationale: The problem tests probability on equally likely ball assignments with parity restrictions. State recursion and binomial incidence counting provide distinct exact routes; their specialized concepts remain in the corresponding methods.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The exact probability is \(\frac14(1-3^{-2022})\), so E is closest. The current prompt, choices, key and supplied reference prompts agree. There is no problem-figure or grading contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The recurrence and incidence count are genuinely different, accessible exact methods. No additional route is needed. The supplied stars-and-bars arguments do not use equally likely outcomes and should not be retained.
review.annotationCheck: Classical probability is appropriately assessed, with parity and multiplication counting supporting. The specialized recursion, geometric-sequence, binomial and double-counting concepts are identified at method level.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The two parity states are exhaustive for an odd total. Among nine ordered placements, three preserve all-odd and two convert one-odd to all-odd. Thus \(p_{k+1}=p_k/9+2/9\); with \(p_0=0\), the stated formula and index 1011 are correct. Since the probability is below 1/4 and every other choice exceeds 1/4, E follows.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 8 and 9 support the exact recurrence. Solution 5 supplies related transitions but only a limiting heuristic; the candidate independently justifies the finite result. The prose is independently organized, and source-informed-original correctly identifies the nonofficial basis.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Adding two balls explains the state choice. The nine-outcome counts, initial condition and repeated division of the deviation are sufficiently explained for an AMC 10 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four IDs are defined and used: state recursion models transitions, cnm_h208 handles the geometric deviation, cnm_h137 handles equally likely placements, and cnm_p156 supports parity.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for classical probability, geometric general terms and odd/even recognition fit their respective steps. The state-recursion synthesis has no supplied CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: F-BF.A.2 and F-LE.A.2 support the geometric-formula component only. The compound-event interpretation overlaps 7.SP.C.8a; this transition calculation does not establish the combination applications of S-CP.B.9. The 2.OA.C.3 link supports elementary parity only. No supplied link covers state-recursion modeling.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The precise recursion node captures the central modeling step, and the remaining nodes provide appropriate supporting concepts.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The incidence set is counted correctly as \(N+2T\). For a fixed bin, choosing its k balls and assigning the rest gives the stated sum. Subtracting the two binomial expansions yields \(2O=N-1\), so \(N+2T=3(N-1)/2\) and \(T=(N-3)/4\). Division by N gives the correct probability and E.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE signed count and AoPS Solution 6 support parity extraction by polynomial evaluations. The incidence equation is an independently developed counting argument. Both references are correctly treated as third-party evidence, with original prose and no official-method claim.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why counting odd bins reveals T. Both counts identify the same pairs and explain their multiplicities. The binomial subtraction explains the cancellation rather than invoking an unexplained sign filter.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h137, cnm_h240, math:double-counting and cnm_p156 all match explicit, necessary parts of the derivation.
